Per-org spend lives in cost-core; max_cost_usd feeds Quarry's flat action-cost table, not LLM spend, so a per-run token budget would be new Model Plane work. Raw observation text enters the prompt unscrubbed, so F-t2-021 should land before default-on.
approachAdjustment: Reword the premise: the in-app browser is not agent-less today because the SPA suggest-action loop works without the flag; the env gate affects the durable run and chat browser_agent autopilot. Put connector-first routing in the parent chat runtime loop (tool descriptions or system prompt in execution-core runtime_loop), since the browser sub-planner never sees provider actions. get_content is already reachable through extract/observe, so widen only press, select, back and wait_for. Move from env flag to org policy only after budgets and grants exist.
verdictReason: The env-gated default-off planner and thin prompt are verified, but the claim that the in-app browser has no real agent is wrong (a flag-free LLM loop exists), get_content is already reachable, and routing belongs in the parent loop; reword and sequence after F-t2-001 and F-t2-021.

The gateway never obtains a grant: create_session posts to Quarry /v1/agent/runs with no grant_id (browser.rs:483-506), which prod Quarry rejects with 403 (agent_routes.rs:1377-1381, main.rs:182-200), and start_ai_run sends the string session:{id} (browser.rs:1235) with data-plane, inference, execution and session bearers but no x-browser-authorization, which model-gateway's VerifiedBrowserBearer extractor requires (browser_run.rs:304, auth.rs:427-437). Missing: a durable store, an issuance path reachable by the gateway, browser-bearer plumbing, run-grant derivation and a prod-mode cross-service test.

constraints: Model Plane owns grant issuance; Quarry only validates (per step) and executes, and domains must come from the broker, never from the client (exact-equality check at agent_routes.rs:314-339). The gateway must not mint authority itself: issuance must go through the broker with the user's delegated browser-audience bearer so org and owner derive from verified claims (server.go AcquireGrant uses the verified principal). The broker is gRPC-only on :9095, so the gateway needs a gRPC client or an HTTP issue endpoint on model-gateway. ZDR: model-gateway already refuses durable browser runs under ZDR, ZDR user sessions that go straight to Quarry still need a grant, and ZDR grants must not be persisted. Grants stay org and owner scoped and a Space must never widen them. A 15-minute broker TTL caps session length until a renewal path exists (see F-t2-011).
approachAdjustment: Placement is right (Model Plane broker plus gateway plumbing, Quarry unchanged). Corrections: (1) the gateway already forwards x-inference-authorization and the data-plane, execution and session bearers on start_ai_run; only x-browser-authorization is missing, so add a browser-bearer parameter to proxy_model_json_with_delegations and mint it through the already-declared BrowserBroker audience. (2) Prefer a model-gateway HTTP endpoint that wraps AcquireGrant, since it already holds the broker client and verified bearer, over teaching the gateway gRPC. (3) create_session, which goes directly to Quarry, needs the grant as well as start_ai_run. (4) Sensitive child grants exist, but deriving a narrower run grant from a session grant is a new broker API. (5) Slice it: issuance, gateway wiring and a prod-mode contract test on the existing in-memory store first, then the Postgres store.
effortNote: Touches the Go broker (store, migration, issue path), model-gateway, gateway proxy plumbing and a prod-mode contract test across four services in three planes; M only holds for the first slice on the in-memory store.
verdictReason: Verified in code: prod Quarry requires a grant on every run and step, nothing in production issues one, the broker store is in memory and the gateway lacks the browser bearer, so every browser path is blocked in prod mode; the plane placement is correct and only details need adjusting.

constraints: Model Plane owns run and session events, so extend model_plane.v1.Event (reserved fields 14-20) instead of introducing a second envelope. Quarry (Ingestion Plane) publishes in that envelope and never writes Model Plane storage; Application Plane projects for realtime; the Frontend gateway only proxies (no cross-plane DB access). ZDR: the envelope carries a zdr flag, ZDR runs stay live-only with no persisted trace, and egress receipts are readable live but the immutable receipt is not retained under ZDR. Request ids must never be used for authorization or tenancy and all Quarry routes stay owner-scoped (caller_owns_live_run). Depends on F-t2-001 for AI-run start.
